profile.reading: Rackspace Belmont NYC2 is the larger of two Rackspace Technology data centers in the Somerset, New Jersey area, sitting roughly 440 meters from the neighboring NYC1 building per this registry's own coordinates. Together the two form what Rackspace's own materials describe as its New York metro data center presence, about an hour from New York City. Rackspace's own resource page for NYC2, fetched directly from rackspace.com, describes a 35,000 square foot facility with 2.7 megawatts of total utility power and 2.4 megawatts of UPS backed power capacity, cooled by 1,100 tons of N+1 redundant cooling capacity, backed by two 1,000 kilowatt diesel generators. The page states the facility carries N+N power redundancy, is carrier neutral with 16 fiber based network carriers, and is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year by trained engineers. Rackspace's own page lists compliance with SSAE18 SOC1, SOC2, and SOC3 audit standards along with PCI DSS, ISO27001, ISO14001, and ISO9001 certifications. A Wikipedia article on Datapipe, the managed hosting company Rackspace acquired in a deal announced September 11, 2017 and completed November 17, 2017, independently documents a Datapipe owned Somerset, New Jersey data center dating back to at least 2009 to 2010, when the company both expanded central New Jersey capacity and committed the Somerset facility to renewable electricity purchased through Constellation NewEnergy's wind program. This lineage is consistent with, though not conclusive proof of, the NYC2 building code's origin, given the close proximity of the two Somerset buildings on what is likely a shared or adjacent campus. No confirmed street address for NYC2 has been found from Rackspace's own materials. The address on file here comes from a reverse geocode of this registry's stored coordinates rather than an operator or government primary source, and should be treated as an approximation pending stronger corroboration. Rackspace Technology is a publicly traded company, NASDAQ ticker RXT, headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, that grew from a 1998 startup into one of the earliest large scale managed hosting and cloud providers, going public in 2008, taken private by Apollo Global Management in 2016, and returning to public markets in 2020.

reading.body:
This facility has published no power capacity figure. The operator's resource page confirms the building exists in Somerset County, New Jersey but provides no megawatt rating, floor area, cooling capacity, or IT load specification. Without a published power budget, the campus cannot be ranked among disclosed capacity in the state or compared to other sites.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities across the registry, of which only 5 publish power capacity totaling 111.3 megawatts. This campus, though confirmed to exist, contributes no disclosed figure to that state total. The site sits approximately 440 meters from a neighboring Rackspace facility also in Somerset County, suggesting a shared or adjacent campus, though the two buildings remain separately documented entries.

The absence of published specifications means this reading cannot assess whether the facility matters to AI infrastructure scaling. The operator has not disclosed the power available to this building, its cooling design, or its certification for GPU-dense workloads. Until specifications are published, the campus remains a mapped location without disclosed technical capacity.
